title: Toileting/Incontinence Crisis
situation: Dad had an accident on the living room couch. He's standing in the middle of the room looking confused and ashamed. His pants are soaked and he keeps saying 'I'm sorry, I'm sorry.' I don't know how to handle this without making him feel worse.

patient_profile.name: Walter
behavioral_patterns: was always very dignified and private
calming_strategies: speaking in a calm matter-of-fact tone
offering his favorite cardigan sweater for comfort
talking about his time in the Navy
safety_concerns: slip and fall risk on wet floors

notes: Must preserve Walter's dignity above all. Should NOT express frustration, disgust, or treat this as a behavioral problem. Should frame incontinence as a brain-body connection issue at this stage. Should suggest matter-of-fact, low-drama approach: 'No big deal, let's get you comfortable.' Recommend contacting doctor if this is a new or worsening pattern (could indicate UTI).
